**Shah Rukh Khan**[[a]](#cite_note-3) (pronounced [[ˈʃaːɦɾʊx xäːn]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu") [ⓘ](/wiki/File:Shahrukh_Khan.ogg "File:Shahrukh Khan.ogg"); born as Shahrukh Khan on 2 November 1965), popularly known by the initials **SRK**, is an [Indian actor](/wiki/Indian_actor "Indian actor") and [film producer](/wiki/Film_producer "Film producer") renowned for his work in [Hindi cinema](/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema"). Referred to in the media as the "[Baadshah](/wiki/Padishah "Padishah") of Bollywood" and "King Khan",[[b]](#cite_note-King-4) he has [appeared in more than 90 films](/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan_filmography "Shah Rukh Khan filmography") and earned [numerous accolades](/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Shah_Rukh_Khan "List of awards and nominations received by Shah Rukh Khan"), including a [National Film Award](/wiki/National_Film_Award "National Film Award") and 15 [Filmfare Awards](/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards").[[3]](#cite_note-5)[[4]](#cite_note-6) He has been awarded the [Padma Shri](/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") by the [Government of India](/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India"), as well as the [Order of Arts and Letters](/wiki/Ordre_des_Arts_et_des_Lettres "Ordre des Arts et des Lettres") and [Legion of Honour](/wiki/Legion_of_Honour "Legion of Honour") by the [Government of France](/wiki/Government_of_France "Government of France"). Khan has a significant following in Asia and among the [Indian diaspora](/wiki/Non-resident_Indian_and_Overseas_Citizen_of_India "Non-resident Indian and Overseas Citizen of India") worldwide.

Referred to in the media as the "[Baadshah](/wiki/Padishah "Padishah") of Bollywood" and "King Khan",[[b]](#cite_note-King-4) he has [appeared in more than 90 films](/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan_filmography "Shah Rukh Khan filmography") and earned [numerous accolades](/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Shah_Rukh_Khan "List of awards and nominations received by Shah Rukh Khan"), including a [National Film Award](/wiki/National_Film_Award "National Film Award") and 15 [Filmfare Awards](/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards").[[3]](#cite_note-5)[[4]](#cite_note-6) He has been awarded the [Padma Shri](/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") by the [Government of India](/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India"), as well as the [Order of Arts and Letters](/wiki/Ordre_des_Arts_et_des_Lettres "Ordre des Arts et des Lettres") and [Legion of Honour](/wiki/Legion_of_Honour "Legion of Honour") by the [Government of France](/wiki/Government_of_France "Government of France"). Khan has a significant following in Asia and among the [Indian diaspora](/wiki/Non-resident_Indian_and_Overseas_Citizen_of_India "Non-resident Indian and Overseas Citizen of India") worldwide.

In terms of audience size and income, several media outlets have described him as one of the most successful film stars in the world.[[c]](#cite_note-biggest-7) Many of his films thematise Indian national identity and connections with diaspora communities, or gender, racial, social and religious differences and grievances.

As of 2015, Khan is co-chairman of the motion picture production company [Red Chillies Entertainment](/wiki/Red_Chillies_Entertainment "Red Chillies Entertainment") and its subsidiaries and is the co-owner of the [Indian Premier League](/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League") cricket team [Kolkata Knight Riders](/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") and the [Caribbean Premier League](/wiki/Caribbean_Premier_League "Caribbean Premier League") team [Trinbago Knight Riders](/wiki/Trinbago_Knight_Riders "Trinbago Knight Riders"). He is a frequent television presenter and stage show performer. Khan's philanthropic endeavours have provided health care and disaster relief, and he was honoured with [UNESCO](/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO")'s Pyramide con Marni award in 2011 for his support of children's education and the [World Economic Forum](/wiki/World_Economic_Forum "World Economic Forum")'s Crystal Award in 2018 for advocating for women's and children's rights in India. He regularly features in listings of the most influential people in [Indian culture](/wiki/Indian_culture "Indian culture"), and in 2008, *[Newsweek](/wiki/Newsweek "Newsweek")* named him one of their fifty most powerful people in the world. In 2022, Khan was voted one of the 50 greatest actors of all time in a readers' poll by *[Empire](/wiki/Empire_(magazine) "Empire (magazine)")*, and in 2023, *[Time](/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")* named him as one of the [most influential people in the world](/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100").[[5]](#cite_note-8)

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text: Khan's father, [Mir](/wiki/Mir_clan "Mir clan") Taj Mohammed Khan, was an [Indian independence](/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement") activist from [Peshawar](/wiki/Peshawar "Peshawar") who campaigned alongside the [Khudai Khidmatgar](/wiki/Khudai_Khidmatgar "Khudai Khidmatgar"), a [nonviolent resistance](/wiki/Nonviolent_resistance "Nonviolent resistance") movement led by [Abdul Ghaffar Khan](/wiki/Abdul_Ghaffar_Khan "Abdul Ghaffar Khan") that sought a [united and independent India](/wiki/Opposition_to_the_partition_of_India "Opposition to the partition of India").[[6]](#cite_note-KoolAgrawal2020-9)[[7]](#cite_note-10) Mir was a follower of Abdul Ghaffar Khan,[[8]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200717–18-11) and affiliated with the [Indian National Congress](/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress").[[9]](#cite_note-ancestral5-12) He was also the cousin of the major general in the [Indian National Army](/wiki/Indian_National_Army "Indian National Army") [Shah Nawaz Khan](/wiki/Shah_Nawaz_Khan_(general) "Shah Nawaz Khan (general)").[[d]](#cite_note-SRKfamily-15) According to Khan, his paternal grandfather, Mir Jan Muhammad Khan, was an ethnic [Pashtun (Pathan)](/wiki/Pashtuns "Pashtuns") from [Afghanistan](/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan").[[12]](#cite_note-16)[[9]](#cite_note-ancestral5-12)[[13]](#cite_note-17) However, his paternal cousins in Peshawar later clarified that the family speaks [Hindko](/wiki/Hindko "Hindko"), a language related to [Punjabi](/wiki/Punjabi_language "Punjabi language") that Khan can understand and speak even if not fluently,[[14]](#cite_note-18) and is originally from [Kashmir](/wiki/Kashmir "Kashmir"), from where they settled in Peshawar centuries back, thus contradicting the claim that his grandfather was a Pashtun from Afghanistan.[[9]](#cite_note-ancestral5-12) As of 2010, Khan's paternal family was still living in the Shah Wali Qataal area of Peshawar's [Qissa Khwani Bazaar](/wiki/Qissa_Khwani_Bazaar "Qissa Khwani Bazaar").[[9]](#cite_note-ancestral5-12)

### Early life

Khan grew up in the [Rajendra Nagar](/wiki/Rajendra_Nagar,_Delhi "Rajendra Nagar, Delhi") neighbourhood of New Delhi.[[25]](#cite_note-30) His father had several business ventures including a restaurant, and the family lived a middle-class life in rented apartments.[[26]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200750-31) Khan attended [St. Columba's School](/wiki/St._Columba%27s_School,_Delhi "St.

Columba's School, Delhi") in central Delhi where he excelled in his studies and in sports such as hockey and football,[[27]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Brien2014217-32) and received the school's highest award, the Sword of Honour.[[26]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200750-31) Initially Khan aspired to pursue a career in sports, however a shoulder injury in his early years meant that he could no longer play.[[28]](#cite_note-33) Instead, in his youth, he acted in stage plays and received praise for his imitations of Bollywood actors, of which his favourites were [Dilip Kumar](/wiki/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar"), [Amitabh Bachchan](/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan"), and [Mumtaz](/wiki/Mumtaz_(Indian_actress) "Mumtaz (Indian actress)").[[29]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200732,_36-34) One of his childhood friends and acting partners was [Amrita Singh](/wiki/Amrita_Singh "Amrita Singh"), who became a [Bollywood](/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") actress.[[30]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200736–38-35) Khan enrolled at [University of Delhi](/wiki/Delhi_University "Delhi University")'s [Hansraj College](/wiki/Hansraj_College "Hansraj College") (1985–88) to earn his bachelor's degree in [economics](/wiki/Economics "Economics"), but spent much of his time at Delhi's Theatre Action Group (TAG),[[31]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200753-36) where he studied acting under the mentorship of theatre director [Barry John](/wiki/Barry_John_(theatre_director) "Barry John (theatre director)").[[32]](#cite_note-37)[[33]](#cite_note-38) After graduating text: ## Acting career

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text: ### 1988–1992: Television and film debut

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text: Khan's first starring role was in [Lekh Tandon](/wiki/Lekh_Tandon "Lekh Tandon")'s television series *Dil Dariya*, which began shooting in 1988, but production delays led to the [Raj Kumar Kapoor](/wiki/Raj_Kumar_Kapoor "Raj Kumar Kapoor") directed 1989 series *[Fauji](/wiki/Fauji_(TV_series) "Fauji (TV series)")* becoming his television debut instead.[[46]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200772–74-52) In the series, which depicted a realistic look at the training of army cadets, he played the leading role of Abhimanyu Rai.[[47]](#cite_note-mumbai-53)[[48]](#cite_note-54) This led to further appearances in [Aziz Mirza](/wiki/Aziz_Mirza "Aziz Mirza")'s television series *[Circus](/wiki/Circus_(Indian_TV_series) "Circus (Indian TV series)")* (1989–90) and [Mani Kaul](/wiki/Mani_Kaul "Mani Kaul")'s miniseries *[Idiot](/wiki/Idiot_(1992_film) "Idiot (1992 film)")* (1992).[[49]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200779–84-55) Khan also played minor parts in the serials *Umeed* (1989) and *[Wagle Ki Duniya](/wiki/Wagle_Ki_Duniya "Wagle Ki Duniya")* (1988–90),[[49]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200779–84-55) and in the English-language [television film](/wiki/Television_film "Television film") *[In Which Annie Gives It Those Ones](/wiki/In_Which_Annie_Gives_It_Those_Ones "In Which Annie Gives It Those Ones")* (1989).[[50]](#cite_note-56) His appearances in these serials led critics to compare his look and acting style with those of the film actor [Dilip Kumar](/wiki/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar"),[[51]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBose200634-57) but Khan was not interested in film acting at the time, thinking that he was not good enough.[[49]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200779–84-55)[[52]](#cite_note-cnnedition-58)

Khan changed his decision to act in films in April 1991,[[53]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200791–96-59) citing it as a way to escape the grief of his mother's death.[[54]](#cite_note-itoday-60) He moved from Delhi to [Mumbai](/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") to pursue a full-time career in Bollywood and was quickly signed to four films.[[53]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200791–96-59) His first offer was for [Hema Malini](/wiki/Hema_Malini "Hema Malini")'s directorial debut *[Dil Aashna Hai](/wiki/Dil_Aashna_Hai "Dil Aashna Hai")*,[[39]](#cite_note-Rediff-Devdas-44)[[47]](#cite_note-mumbai-53) and by June, he had started his first shoot.[[55]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200797-61) His film debut was in *[Deewana](/wiki/Deewana_(1992_film) "Deewana (1992 film)")*, which was released in June 1992.[[56]](#cite_note-62) In it he starred alongside [Divya Bharti](/wiki/Divya_Bharti "Divya Bharti") as the second male lead behind [Rishi Kapoor](/wiki/Rishi_Kapoor "Rishi Kapoor").

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text:
Khan changed his decision to act in films in April 1991,[[53]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200791–96-59) citing it as a way to escape the grief of his mother's death.[[54]](#cite_note-itoday-60) He moved from Delhi to [Mumbai](/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") to pursue a full-time career in Bollywood and was quickly signed to four films.[[53]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200791–96-59) His first offer was for [Hema Malini](/wiki/Hema_Malini "Hema Malini")'s directorial debut *[Dil Aashna Hai](/wiki/Dil_Aashna_Hai "Dil Aashna Hai")*,[[39]](#cite_note-Rediff-Devdas-44)[[47]](#cite_note-mumbai-53) and by June, he had started his first shoot.[[55]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra200797-61) His film debut was in *[Deewana](/wiki/Deewana_(1992_film) "Deewana (1992 film)")*, which was released in June 1992.[[56]](#cite_note-62) In it he starred alongside [Divya Bharti](/wiki/Divya_Bharti "Divya Bharti") as the second male lead behind [Rishi Kapoor](/wiki/Rishi_Kapoor "Rishi Kapoor").

*Deewana* became a box office hit and launched Khan's Bollywood career;[[57]](#cite_note-63) he earned the [Filmfare Best Male Debut Award](/wiki/Filmfare_Best_Male_Debut_Award "Filmfare Best Male Debut Award") for his performance.[[58]](#cite_note-toi-awards-64) Also released in 1992 were Khan's first films as the male lead, *[Chamatkar](/wiki/Chamatkar "Chamatkar")*, *Dil Aashna Hai*, and the comedy *[Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman](/wiki/Raju_Ban_Gaya_Gentleman "Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman")*, which was his first of many collaborations with the actress [Juhi Chawla](/wiki/Juhi_Chawla "Juhi Chawla").[[59]](#cite_note-65) His initial film roles saw him play characters who displayed energy and enthusiasm. According to Arnab Ray of *[Daily News and Analysis](/wiki/Daily_News_and_Analysis "Daily News and Analysis")*, Khan brought a new kind of acting as he was "sliding down stairs on a slab of ice, cartwheeling, somersaulting, lips trembling, eyes trembling, bringing to the screen the kind of physical energy... visceral, intense, maniacal one moment and cloyingly boyish the next."[[60]](#cite_note-DNA-66)

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text:
### 1993–1994: Negative characters

Among his 1993 releases, Khan garnered the most appreciation for portraying villainous roles in two box office hits: a murderer in *[Baazigar](/wiki/Baazigar "Baazigar")*, and an obsessive lover in *[Darr](/wiki/Darr "Darr")*.[[61]](#cite_note-67) The former, in which Khan played an ambiguous avenger who murders his girlfriend, shocked Indian audiences with an unexpected violation of the standard Bollywood formula.[[62]](#cite_note-68) In *The Cambridge Companion to Modern Indian Culture*, Sonal Khullar called the character "the consummate [anti-hero](/wiki/Antihero "Antihero")".[[63]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDalmiaSadana2012180-69) His performance in *Baazigar*, which would be his first of many appearances with actress [Kajol](/wiki/Kajol "Kajol"), won Khan his first [Filmfare Award for Best Actor](/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Actor").[[64]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGulazāraNihalaniChatterjee2003574-70) In 2003, the *[Encyclopaedia of Hindi Cinema](/wiki/Encyclopaedia_of_Hindi_Cinema "Encyclopaedia of Hindi Cinema")* stated that Khan "defied the image of the conventional hero in both these films and created his own version of the revisionist hero".[[64]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGulazāraNihalaniChatterjee2003574-70) *Darr* marked the first of Khan's many collaborations with filmmaker [Yash Chopra](/wiki/Yash_Chopra "Yash Chopra") and his company [Yash Raj Films](/wiki/Yash_Raj_Films "Yash Raj Films").

Khan's stammering and the use of the phrase "I love you, K-k-k-Kiran" were popular with audiences.[[65]](#cite_note-71) Malini Mannath of *The Indian Express* argued that he "walks away with the acting honours in yet another negative role".[[66]](#cite_note-72) For *Darr* he received a nomination for the [Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Negative Role](/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_a_Negative_Role "Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Negative Role"), also known as the Best Villain Award, but lost to [Paresh Rawal](/wiki/Paresh_Rawal "Paresh Rawal") for *[Sir](/wiki/Sir_(1993_film) "Sir (1993 film)")*.[[67]](#cite_note-FFAwardsPDF-73) Also in 1993, Khan performed a nude scene with [Deepa Sahi](/wiki/Deepa_Sahi "Deepa Sahi") in *[Maya Memsaab](/wiki/Maya_Memsaab "Maya Memsaab")*, although parts of it were censored by the [Central Board of Film Certification](/wiki/Central_Board_of_Film_Certification "Central Board of Film Certification").[[68]](#cite_note-74) The ensuing controversy prompted him to eschew such scenes in future roles.[[69]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChandra2008110–111-75)

In 1994, Khan played a love-struck musician in [Kundan Shah](/wiki/Kundan_Shah "Kundan Shah")'s comedy-drama film *[Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa](/wiki/Kabhi_Haan_Kabhi_Naa "Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa")* opposite [Deepak Tijori](/wiki/Deepak_Tijori "Deepak Tijori") and [Suchitra Krishnamurthy](/wiki/Suchitra_Krishnamurthy "Suchitra Krishnamurthy"), which he later professed was his favourite role. His performance earned him a [Filmfare Critics Award for Best Performance](/wiki/Filmfare_Critics_Award_for_Best_Actor#Filmfare_Critics_Award_for_Best_Performance "Filmfare Critics Award for Best Actor"), and in a retrospective review from 2004, [Sukanya Verma](/wiki/Sukanya_Verma "Sukanya Verma") of [Rediff.com](/wiki/Rediff.com "Rediff.com") referred to it as Khan's best performance, calling him "spontaneous, vulnerable, boyish, mischievous and acting straight from the heart".[[70]](#cite_note-bestperf-76) Also in 1994, Khan won the [Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Negative Role](/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_a_Negative_Role "Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Negative Role") for his role as an obsessive lover in *[Anjaam](/wiki/Anjaam "Anjaam")*, co-starring [Madhuri Dixit](/wiki/Madhuri_Dixit "Madhuri Dixit").[[64]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGulazāraNihalaniChatterjee2003574-70) At the time, playing antagonistic roles was considered risky to a leading man's career in mainstream Hindi cinema. Arnab Ray subsequently credited Khan for taking "insane risks" and "pushing the envelope" by choosing to play such characters, through which he established his career.[[60]](#cite_note-DNA-66) The director [Mukul S. Anand](/wiki/Mukul_S._Anand "Mukul S. Anand") called him "the new face of the industry" at the time.[[54]](#cite_note-itoday-60)

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text:
### 1995–1998: Romantic roles

[![Shah Rukh Khan hugs Kajol](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Shah_Rukh_Khan_%26_Kajol_unveil_the_special_coffee_table_book_%27DDLJ%27.jpg/250px-Shah_Rukh_Khan_%26_Kajol_unveil_the_special_coffee_table_book_%27DDLJ%27.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](/wiki/File:Shah_Rukh_Khan_%26_Kajol_unveil_the_special_coffee_table_book_%27DDLJ%27.jpg)

Khan starred in seven films in 1995, the first of which was [Rakesh Roshan](/wiki/Rakesh_Roshan "Rakesh Roshan")'s melodramatic thriller *[Karan Arjun](/wiki/Karan_Arjun "Karan Arjun")*. Co-starring [Salman Khan](/wiki/Salman_Khan "Salman Khan") and Kajol, it became the second-highest-grossing film of the year in India.[[71]](#cite_note-g1995-77) His most significant release that year was [Aditya Chopra](/wiki/Aditya_Chopra "Aditya Chopra")'s directorial debut, the romance *[Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge](/wiki/Dilwale_Dulhania_Le_Jayenge "Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge")*, in which he played a young [Non-resident Indian](/wiki/Non-resident_Indian_and_person_of_Indian_origin "Non-resident Indian and person of Indian origin") (NRI) who falls in love with Kajol's character during a trip across Europe.

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text:
Khan starred in seven films in 1995, the first of which was [Rakesh Roshan](/wiki/Rakesh_Roshan "Rakesh Roshan")'s melodramatic thriller *[Karan Arjun](/wiki/Karan_Arjun "Karan Arjun")*. Co-starring [Salman Khan](/wiki/Salman_Khan "Salman Khan") and Kajol, it became the second-highest-grossing film of the year in India.[[71]](#cite_note-g1995-77) His most significant release that year was [Aditya Chopra](/wiki/Aditya_Chopra "Aditya Chopra")'s directorial debut, the romance *[Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge](/wiki/Dilwale_Dulhania_Le_Jayenge "Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge")*, in which he played a young [Non-resident Indian](/wiki/Non-resident_Indian_and_person_of_Indian_origin "Non-resident Indian and person of Indian origin") (NRI) who falls in love with Kajol's character during a trip across Europe.

Khan was initially reticent to portray the role of a lover, but this film is credited with establishing him as a "romantic hero".[[72]](#cite_note-78) Lauded by both critics and the public, it became the year's highest grossing production in India and abroad and was declared an "all time blockbuster" by [Box Office India](/wiki/Box_Office_India "Box Office India"),[[71]](#cite_note-g1995-77)[[73]](#cite_note-79) with an estimated lifetime gross of ₹2 billion (US$61.68 million) worldwide.[[74]](#cite_note-Rajinder-80)[[75]](#cite_note-Ganti-81) It is the longest-running film in the history of Indian cinema; it is still showing at the [Maratha Mandir](/wiki/Maratha_Mandir "Maratha Mandir") theatre in Mumbai after more than 1000 weeks as of early 2015.[[76]](#cite_note-82)[[77]](#cite_note-83) The film won ten [Filmfare Awards](/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards"), including the second of Khan's Best Actor Awards.[[64]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGulazāraNihalaniChatterjee2003574-70) The director and critic [Raja Sen](/wiki/Raja_Sen "Raja Sen") said, "Khan gives a fabulous performance, redefining the lover for the 1990s with great panache. He's cool and flippant, but sincere enough to appeal to the [audience]. The performance itself is, like the best in the business, played well enough to come across as effortless, as non-acting."[[78]](#cite_note-84)

In 1996, all four of Khan's releases failed critically and commercially,[[79]](#cite_note-85) but the following year, his starring role opposite [Aditya Pancholi](/wiki/Aditya_Pancholi "Aditya Pancholi") and Juhi Chawla in Aziz Mirza's romantic comedy *[Yes Boss](/wiki/Yes_Boss_(film) "Yes Boss (film)")* earned him accolades that included a Filmfare Best Actor nomination.[[67]](#cite_note-FFAwardsPDF-73) Later in 1997, he starred in [Subhash Ghai](/wiki/Subhash_Ghai "Subhash Ghai")'s diasporic-themed social drama *[Pardes](/wiki/Pardes_(1997_film) "Pardes (1997 film)")*,[[80]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHirji2010110-86) portraying Arjun, a musician facing a moral dilemma. *[India Today](/wiki/India_Today "India Today")* cites it as one of the first major Bollywood pictures to succeed in the United States.[[81]](#cite_note-87) Khan's final release of 1997 was the second collaboration with Yash Chopra in the popular musical romance *[Dil To Pagal Hai](/wiki/Dil_To_Pagal_Hai "Dil To Pagal Hai")*. He portrayed Rahul, a stage director caught in a [love triangle](/wiki/Love_triangle "Love triangle") between Madhuri Dixit and [Karisma Kapoor](/wiki/Karisma_Kapoor "Karisma Kapoor"). The film and his performance met with critical praise, winning Khan his third Best Actor Award at Filmfare.[[64]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGulazāraNihalaniChatterjee2003574-70)

The roles in this phase of his career, and the series of romantic comedies and family dramas that followed, earned Khan widespread adulation from audiences, particularly teenagers,[[89]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTERaj2009143-95) and according to the author [Anupama Chopra](/wiki/Anupama_Chopra "Anupama Chopra"), established him as an icon of romance in India.[[90]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra2007112-96)[[91]](#cite_note-romantic_hero-97) He continued to have frequent professional associations with [Yash Chopra](/wiki/Yash_Chopra "Yash Chopra"), Aditya Chopra, and [Karan Johar](/wiki/Karan_Johar "Karan Johar"), who moulded his image and made him into a superstar.[[92]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra2007124–125-98) Khan became a romantic leading man without ever actually kissing any of his co-stars,[[90]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra2007112-96) although he broke this rule in 2012, after strong urging by Yash Chopra.[[93]](#cite_note-kiss-99)

Pyaar Hai")*, starring [Hrithik Roshan](/wiki/Hrithik_Roshan "Hrithik Roshan"), then a newcomer, who critics believed overshadowed Khan.[[97]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra2007181–190-103) Swapna Mitter of Rediff.com spoke of Khan's predictable mannerisms, saying "Frankly, it's high time he innovated his act a little."[[98]](#cite_note-104) Khan did a supporting role in [Kamal Haasan](/wiki/Kamal_Haasan "Kamal Haasan")'s *[Hey Ram](/wiki/Hey_Ram "Hey Ram")* (2000), which was made simultaneously in [Tamil](/wiki/Tamil_language "Tamil language") and [Hindi](/wiki/Hindi "Hindi").

text:
In 2002, Khan played the title role as a rebellious alcoholic opposite Aishwarya Rai and Madhuri Dixit in [Sanjay Leela Bhansali](/wiki/Sanjay_Leela_Bhansali "Sanjay Leela Bhansali")'s period romance *[Devdas](/wiki/Devdas_(2002_Hindi_film) "Devdas (2002 Hindi film)")*.

At a cost of over ₹500 million (US$10.29 million), it was the most expensive Bollywood film ever made at the time,[[116]](#cite_note-122) and became a box office success, earning approximately ₹1.68 billion ($35 million) worldwide.[[117]](#cite_note-indiatoday-123) The film earned numerous accolades including 10 Filmfare Awards, with Best Actor for Khan,[[58]](#cite_note-toi-awards-64) and a [BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language](/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Film_Not_in_the_English_Language "BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language").[[118]](#cite_note-124) Khan next starred in *[Kal Ho Naa Ho](/wiki/Kal_Ho_Naa_Ho "Kal Ho Naa Ho")* (2003), a comedy-drama written by Karan Johar and set in New York City, which became the second-highest-grossing film domestically and the top-grossing Bollywood film in external markets that year.[[110]](#cite_note-overseas-116)[[119]](#cite_note-2003_BO-125) Co-starring with [Jaya Bachchan](/wiki/Jaya_Bachchan "Jaya Bachchan"), [Saif Ali Khan](/wiki/Saif_Ali_Khan "Saif Ali Khan"), and [Preity Zinta](/wiki/Preity_Zinta "Preity Zinta"), Khan received critical praise for his portrayal of Aman Mathur, a man with a fatal heart disease, with critics praising his emotional impact upon audiences.[[120]](#cite_note-126) Conflict broke out between Khan and the other partners of Dreamz Unlimited over the failure to cast Juhi Chawla in their 2003 production of Aziz Mirza's *[Chalte Chalte](/wiki/Chalte_Chalte_(2003_film) "Chalte Chalte (2003 film)")*, and they parted ways, despite the film's success.[[121]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra2007194–195-127)

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text:
### 2004–2009: Comeback

2004 was a critically and commercially successful year for Khan. He transformed Dreamz Unlimited into [Red Chillies Entertainment](/wiki/Red_Chillies_Entertainment "Red Chillies Entertainment"), adding his wife Gauri as a producer.[[122]](#cite_note-RedCh-128) In the company's first production, he starred in [Farah Khan](/wiki/Farah_Khan "Farah Khan")'s directorial debut, the [masala film](/wiki/Masala_film "Masala film") *[Main Hoon Na](/wiki/Main_Hoon_Na "Main Hoon Na")*. A fictionalised account of [India–Pakistan relations](/wiki/India%E2%80%93Pakistan_relations "India–Pakistan relations"), it was viewed by some commentators as a conscious effort to move away from the stereotypical portrayal of Pakistan as the constant villain.[[123]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBharatKumar201243-129) Khan then played an Indian Air Force pilot who falls in love with a Pakistani woman (Preity Zinta) in Yash Chopra's romance film *[Veer-Zaara](/wiki/Veer-Zaara "Veer-Zaara")*, which was screened at the [55th Berlin Film Festival](/wiki/Berlin_International_Film_Festival "Berlin International Film Festival") to critical praise.[[124]](#cite_note-130) It was the highest earning film of 2004 in India, with a worldwide gross of over ₹940 million (US$20.74 million), and *Main Hoon Na* was the second-highest earner with ₹680 million (US$15.01 million).[[115]](#cite_note-Worldwide_gross-121)[[125]](#cite_note-2004_BO-131)

In his final release of 2004, Khan starred as a [NASA](/wiki/NASA "NASA") scientist who patriotically returns to India to rekindle his roots in [Ashutosh Gowariker](/wiki/Ashutosh_Gowariker "Ashutosh Gowariker")'s social drama *[Swades](/wiki/Swades "Swades")* (meaning "Homeland"), which became the first Indian picture to be shot inside the NASA research centre at the [Kennedy Space Center](/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center") in Florida.[[126]](#cite_note-Hindustan0314-132) Film scholar Stephen Teo refers to the picture as an example of "Bollywoodised realism", displaying a transcendence in conventional narrative and audience expectation in Hindi cinema.[[127]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETeo2013123-133) In December 2013, *The Times of India* reported that Khan found filming the picture such an emotionally overwhelming and life-changing experience that he had still not viewed the film.[[128]](#cite_note-134) [Derek Elley](/wiki/Derek_Elley "Derek Elley") of *[Variety](/wiki/Variety_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")* found Khan's performance "unsettling" as "a self-satisfied expatriate determined to bring Western values to poor Indian peasants",[[129]](#cite_note-135) but several film critics, including Jitesh Pillai, believed it to have been his finest acting to date.[[130]](#cite_note-rediffswades-136)[[131]](#cite_note-137) He was nominated for the Filmfare Best Actor Award for all three of his 2004 releases and eventually won the award for *Swades*.[[58]](#cite_note-toi-awards-64)[[67]](#cite_note-FFAwardsPDF-73) *[Filmfare](/wiki/Filmfare "Filmfare")* later included his performance in the 2010 issue of Bollywood's "Top 80 Iconic Performances".[[132]](#cite_note-iconic-138)

In 2005, Khan starred in [Amol Palekar](/wiki/Amol_Palekar "Amol Palekar")'s fantasy drama, *[Paheli](/wiki/Paheli_(2005_film) "Paheli (2005 film)")*. The film was India's submission for the Best Foreign Language Film at the [79th Academy Awards](/wiki/79th_Academy_Awards "79th Academy Awards").[[133]](#cite_note-139) He later collaborated with Karan Johar for the third time in the musical romantic drama *[Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna](/wiki/Kabhi_Alvida_Naa_Kehna "Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna")* (2006), in which he played an unhappily married man who has an extramarital affair with a married woman. The film, which featured an ensemble cast including Amitabh Bachchan, [Abhishek Bachchan](/wiki/Abhishek_Bachchan "Abhishek Bachchan"), Rani Mukerji, Preity Zinta and [Kirron Kher](/wiki/Kirron_Kher "Kirron Kher"), emerged as India's highest-grossing film in the overseas market,[[110]](#cite_note-overseas-116) earning more than ₹1.13 billion (US$25.62 million) worldwide.[[115]](#cite_note-Worldwide_gross-121) Both his roles in *[Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna](/wiki/Kabhi_Alvida_Naa_Kehna "Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna")* and the action film *[Don](/wiki/Don_(2006_Hindi_film) "Don (2006 Hindi film)")*, a remake of the [1978 film of the same name](/wiki/Don_(1978_film) "Don (1978 film)"), earned Khan Best Actor nominations at the Filmfare Awards,[[134]](#cite_note-140) despite his performance as the [titular character](/wiki/Don_(character) "Don (character)") in *Don* being negatively compared to that of Amitabh Bachchan in the original film.[[135]](#cite_note-taran-141)[[136]](#cite_note-142)

In 2007, Khan portrayed a disgraced hockey player who coached the [Indian women's national hockey team](/wiki/India_women%27s_national_field_hockey_team "India women's national field hockey team") to World Cup success in Yash Raj Films' semi-fictional *[Chak De! India](/wiki/Chak_De!_India "Chak De! India")*. Bhaichand Patel notes that Khan, who had a background in the sport playing for his university's hockey team,[[138]](#cite_note-144) essentially portrayed himself as a "cosmopolitan, liberal, Indian Muslim".[[139]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPatel2012245-145) Faring well in both India and abroad,[[115]](#cite_note-Worldwide_gross-121)[[140]](#cite_note-director-146) Khan garnered another Filmfare Award for Best Actor for his performance,[[58]](#cite_note-toi-awards-64) which [Rajeev Masand](/wiki/Rajeev_Masand "Rajeev Masand") of [CNN-IBN](/wiki/CNN-IBN "CNN-IBN") considers to have been "without any of his typical trappings, without any of his trademark quirks", portraying Kabir Khan "like a real flesh-and-blood human being".[[141]](#cite_note-typicalactingstyle-147) *Filmfare* included his performance in their 2010 issue of the "Top 80 Iconic Performances".[[142]](#cite_note-Filmfare-148) In the same year, Khan starred alongside [Arjun Rampal](/wiki/Arjun_Rampal "Arjun Rampal"), [Deepika Padukone](/wiki/Deepika_Padukone "Deepika Padukone") and [Shreyas Talpade](/wiki/Shreyas_Talpade "Shreyas Talpade") in Farah Khan's reincarnation melodrama *[Om Shanti Om](/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om "Om Shanti Om")*, portraying a 1970s junior artiste who is reborn as a 2000s era superstar.

Khan collaborated for the third time with Aditya Chopra on the romantic comedy *[Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi](/wiki/Rab_Ne_Bana_Di_Jodi "Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi")* (2008) opposite debutante [Anushka Sharma](/wiki/Anushka_Sharma "Anushka Sharma"). He played Surinder Sahni, a shy man with low self-esteem, whose love for his young arranged wife (Sharma) causes him to transform himself into Raj, a boisterous alter-ego. Rachel Saltz of *[The New York Times](/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* believed the dual role to have been "tailor-made" for Khan, allowing him to display his talents,[[146]](#cite_note-152) although Deep Contractor from *Epilogue* thought Khan displayed greater strength in the role of Surinder and weakness in the role of monologue-prone Raj.[[147]](#cite_note-153) In December 2008, Khan suffered a shoulder injury while filming a small role in [Mudassar Aziz](/wiki/Mudassar_Aziz "Mudassar Aziz")'s *[Dulha Mil Gaya](/wiki/Dulha_Mil_Gaya "Dulha Mil Gaya")*.

The company covered up the offending word on billboards that had already been installed with the original title.[[151]](#cite_note-157)

### 2010–2014: Expansion to action and comedy

[![Shah Rukh Khan with Kajol and Karan Johar](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/SRK_Kajol_%26_Karan.jpg/250px-SRK_Kajol_%26_Karan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](/wiki/File:SRK_Kajol_%26_Karan.jpg)

With director [Karan Johar](/wiki/Karan_Johar "Karan Johar") and co-star Kajol at an event for *[My Name Is Khan](/wiki/My_Name_Is_Khan "My Name Is Khan")* in 2010

After refusing the role that subsequently went to [Anil Kapoor](/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor") in [Danny Boyle](/wiki/Danny_Boyle "Danny Boyle")'s *[Slumdog Millionaire](/wiki/Slumdog_Millionaire "Slumdog Millionaire")* (2008), Khan began shooting *[My Name Is Khan](/wiki/My_Name_Is_Khan "My Name Is Khan")* (2010), his fourth collaboration with director Karan Johar and his sixth with Kajol.[[152]](#cite_note-158) The film is based on a true story and set against the backdrop of perceptions of Islam after the [11 September attacks](/wiki/11_September_attacks "11 September attacks").

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text:
After refusing the role that subsequently went to [Anil Kapoor](/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor") in [Danny Boyle](/wiki/Danny_Boyle "Danny Boyle")'s *[Slumdog Millionaire](/wiki/Slumdog_Millionaire "Slumdog Millionaire")* (2008), Khan began shooting *[My Name Is Khan](/wiki/My_Name_Is_Khan "My Name Is Khan")* (2010), his fourth collaboration with director Karan Johar and his sixth with Kajol.[[152]](#cite_note-158) The film is based on a true story and set against the backdrop of perceptions of Islam after the [11 September attacks](/wiki/11_September_attacks "11 September attacks").

Khan plays Rizwan Khan, a Muslim suffering from mild [Asperger syndrome](/wiki/Asperger_syndrome "Asperger syndrome") who sets out on a journey across America to meet the country's president, a role that film scholar Stephen Teo sees as a "symbol of assertive [rasa](/wiki/Rasa_(aesthetics) "Rasa (aesthetics)") values" and another example of Khan representing NRI identity in global Bollywood.[[153]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETeo2013125-159) To provide an accurate portrayal of a sufferer without disparagement, Khan spent several months researching his role by reading books, watching videos and talking to people affected by the condition.[[154]](#cite_note-160)[[155]](#cite_note-161) Upon release, *My Name is Khan* became one of the highest grossing Bollywood films of all time outside India,[[115]](#cite_note-Worldwide_gross-121)[[110]](#cite_note-overseas-116) and earned Khan his eighth Filmfare Award for Best Actor,[[58]](#cite_note-toi-awards-64) equalling the record for the most wins in the category with [Dilip Kumar](/wiki/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar").[[156]](#cite_note-FF8-162) Jay Wesissberg from *Variety* noted how Khan portrayed the Asperger's sufferer with "averted eyes, springy steps, [and] stuttered repetitions of memorized texts", believing it to have been a "standout performance sure to receive the Autism Society's gold seal of approval".[[157]](#cite_note-163)

In 2011, Khan starred alongside Arjun Rampal and Kareena Kapoor in [Anubhav Sinha](/wiki/Anubhav_Sinha "Anubhav Sinha")'s superhero film *[Ra.One](/wiki/Ra.One "Ra.One")*, his first work in this subgenre, as a favour to his children.[[158]](#cite_note-geo-164) The film follows the story of a London-based video game designer who creates a villainous character who escapes into the real world.

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text:
In 2011, Khan starred alongside Arjun Rampal and Kareena Kapoor in [Anubhav Sinha](/wiki/Anubhav_Sinha "Anubhav Sinha")'s superhero film *[Ra.One](/wiki/Ra.One "Ra.One")*, his first work in this subgenre, as a favour to his children.[[158]](#cite_note-geo-164) The film follows the story of a London-based video game designer who creates a villainous character who escapes into the real world.

It was billed as Bollywood's most expensive production; it had an estimated budget of ₹1.25 billion (US$26.78 million).[[159]](#cite_note-165)[[160]](#cite_note-expensiveBW-166) Despite negative media coverage of the film's box office performance, *Ra.One* was a financial success with a gross of ₹2.4 billion (US$51.42 million).[[161]](#cite_note-wgross-167)[[162]](#cite_note-cnngrossraone-168) The film, and Khan's portrayal of a dual role, received mixed reviews; while most critics praised his performance as the robotic superhero G.One, they criticised his portrayal of the video game designer Shekhar.[[163]](#cite_note-169) Khan's second release of 2011 was *[Don 2](/wiki/Don_2 "Don 2")*, a sequel to *Don* (2006).[[164]](#cite_note-170) To prepare for his role, Khan exercised extensively as he performed most of the stunts himself.[[165]](#cite_note-171) His performance earned him positive reviews from critics; [Nikhat Kazmi](/wiki/Nikhat_Kazmi "Nikhat Kazmi") of *[The Times of India](/wiki/The_Times_of_India "The Times of India")* said, "Shah Rukh remains in command and never loses his foothold, neither through the dramatic sequences nor through the action cuts".[[166]](#cite_note-172) The year's highest grossing Bollywood production abroad,[[167]](#cite_note-173)[[168]](#cite_note-Box_Office_India-174) it was showcased at the [62nd Berlin International Film Festival](/wiki/62nd_Berlin_International_Film_Festival "62nd Berlin International Film Festival").[[169]](#cite_note-175)

Khan's only release in 2012 was Yash Chopra's [swan song](/wiki/Swan_song "Swan song"),[[170]](#cite_note-176) the romantic drama *[Jab Tak Hai Jaan](/wiki/Jab_Tak_Hai_Jaan "Jab Tak Hai Jaan")*, which saw him once again in a romantic role, starring opposite [Katrina Kaif](/wiki/Katrina_Kaif "Katrina Kaif") and Anushka Sharma. CNN-IBN considered the overall performance by Khan to have been one of his finest to date, but believed that Khan's first screen kiss of his career with Katrina Kaif, twenty years his junior, was an awkward one.[[93]](#cite_note-kiss-99)[[171]](#cite_note-177) *Jab Tak Hai Jaan* was a moderate financial success earning over ₹2.11 billion (US$39.49 million) worldwide.[[172]](#cite_note-178)[[173]](#cite_note-Grosstwo-179) The film was showcased at the 2012 [Marrakech International Film Festival](/wiki/Marrakech_International_Film_Festival "Marrakech International Film Festival") in Morocco, along with *Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham*, *Veer-Zaara*, and *Don 2*.[[174]](#cite_note-MIFF-180) At the following [Zee Cine Awards](/wiki/Zee_Cine_Awards "Zee Cine Awards"), Khan performed a tribute to the late Yash Chopra along with Kaif, Sharma, and several of Chopra's other past heroines.[[175]](#cite_note-181)

Khan next appeared alongside Kajol, [Varun Dhawan](/wiki/Varun_Dhawan "Varun Dhawan") and [Kriti Sanon](/wiki/Kriti_Sanon "Kriti Sanon") in Rohit Shetty's action comedy *[Dilwale](/wiki/Dilwale_(2015_film) "Dilwale (2015 film)")* (2015). The film garnered mixed reviews, though it was financially profitable with a gross of ₹3.7 billion (US$57.68 million).[[186]](#cite_note-192) [Namrata Joshi](/wiki/Namrata_Joshi "Namrata Joshi") of *The Hindu* commented, "With *Dilwale*, Rohit Shetty goes hopelessly wrong despite much that he had at his disposal, including a power-packed cast and producer", and felt that the attempt to repackage Khan and Kajol had backfired.[[187]](#cite_note-193) He then took on dual parts of a superstar and his doppelgänger fan in [Maneesh Sharma](/wiki/Maneesh_Sharma "Maneesh Sharma")'s action thriller *[Fan](/wiki/Fan_(2016_film) "Fan (2016 film)")* (2016). [Peter Bradshaw](/wiki/Peter_Bradshaw "Peter Bradshaw") of *[The Guardian](/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* considered the film to be "exhausting, bizarre yet watchable" and thought that Khan was aptly "creepy" as the obsessive admirer.[[188]](#cite_note-194) The film underperformed at the box office, and trade journalists attributed this failure to the film's non-conformity to mainstream formula.[[189]](#cite_note-195) Later that year, Khan portrayed the supporting part of a therapist to an aspiring cinematographer ([Alia Bhatt](/wiki/Alia_Bhatt "Alia Bhatt")) in [Gauri Shinde](/wiki/Gauri_Shinde "Gauri Shinde")'s coming-of-age film *[Dear Zindagi](/wiki/Dear_Zindagi "Dear Zindagi")*.[[190]](#cite_note-196)

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text: ### 2023–present: Resurgence

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text: In 2023, Khan reunited with Yash Raj Films in the action thriller *[Pathaan](/wiki/Pathaan_(film) "Pathaan (film)")* (2023), set in the [YRF Spy Universe](/wiki/YRF_Spy_Universe "YRF Spy Universe"), in which he played an exiled field agent assigned to stop a terrorist attack in India.[[206]](#cite_note-212) Critic Sukanya Verma took note of Khan's "weathered intensity, grizzly charisma and trademark wit", while [Kaveree Bamzai](/wiki/Kaveree_Bamzai "Kaveree Bamzai") termed it a "much-needed makeover" of an ageing Khan into an action star.[[207]](#cite_note-213)[[208]](#cite_note-214) *Pathaan* broke several box-office records, thus re-establishing Khan's stardom.[[209]](#cite_note-215)[[210]](#cite_note-216) Khan took on another action film role in the same year in [Atlee](/wiki/Atlee_(director) "Atlee (director)")'s *[Jawan](/wiki/Jawan_(film) "Jawan (film)")*, playing father and son doppelgängers.[[211]](#cite_note-217) Nandini Ramnath of *[Scroll.in](/wiki/Scroll.in "Scroll.in")* wrote that "Khan's screen image – expansive, suffused with love, heroic in an old-fashioned way without being aggressively macho, irreverent but also sincere – helps sell a conceit that might have crashed with any other actor".[[212]](#cite_note-218) *Jawan* broke the records set by *Pathaan*.[[213]](#cite_note-219) Both films grossed over ₹10 billion (US$100 million) to rank, respectively, as Hindi cinema's second and third biggest grossers worldwide,[[214]](#cite_note-220) making Khan the first Indian actor to deliver two films that earned over ₹10 billion.[[215]](#cite_note-221) For his performance in *Jawan*, he received his first [National Film Award](/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards") for [Best Actor in a Leading Role](/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Leading_Role "National Film Award for Best Actor in a Leading Role").[[216]](#cite_note-:4-222)[[217]](#cite_note-223)

In his final release of 2023, Khan starred in [Rajkumar Hirani](/wiki/Rajkumar_Hirani "Rajkumar Hirani")'s *[Dunki](/wiki/Dunki_(film) "Dunki (film)")*, a social drama about an [illegal immigration](/wiki/Illegal_immigration "Illegal immigration") technique named [donkey flight](/wiki/Donkey_flight "Donkey flight").[[218]](#cite_note-224)[[219]](#cite_note-225) Uday Bhatia wrote that his role as a "romantic feminist soldier patriot friend" marked "a break from Khan the action star but offers no respite from the Khan the perfect screen idol".[[220]](#cite_note-226) Grossing over ₹4.7 billion (US$49 million), *Dunki* emerged as Khan's third consecutive commercial success of the year, although it did not match up to the record grosses of *Pathaan* or *Jawan*.[[221]](#cite_note-227)

Khan co-produced three films from 1999 to 2003 as a founding member of the partnership Dreamz Unlimited.[[95]](#cite_note-dreamz-101) After the partnership was dissolved, he and Gauri restructured the company as Red Chillies Entertainment,[[122]](#cite_note-RedCh-128) which includes divisions dealing with film and television production, visual effects, and advertising.[[223]](#cite_note-229) As of 2015, the company has produced or co-produced at least nine films.[[224]](#cite_note-230) Either Khan or Gauri are usually given production credits, and he has appeared in most of the films, either in the lead role, or in a guest appearance. Khan was involved in several aspects of the making of *Ra.One* (2011). Aside from acting, he produced the film, volunteered to write the console game script, dubbed for it, oversaw its technical development, and wrote the digital comics based on the film's characters.[[225]](#cite_note-231)[[226]](#cite_note-ET-232) Khan has occasionally done [playback singing](/wiki/Playback_singer "Playback singer") for his films. In *Josh* (2000) he sang the popular song "Apun Bola Tu Meri Laila". He also sang in *Don* (2006) and *Jab Tak Hai Jaan* (2012).[[227]](#cite_note-233) For *[Always Kabhi Kabhi](/wiki/Always_Kabhi_Kabhi "Always Kabhi Kabhi")* (2011), which was produced by Red Chillies, Khan participated in the lyrical composition.[[228]](#cite_note-234)

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text:
### Ownership of Kolkata Knight Riders

In 2008, Khan, in partnership with Juhi Chawla and her husband [Jay Mehta](/wiki/Jay_Mehta "Jay Mehta"), acquired ownership rights for the franchise representing [Kolkata](/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata") in the [Twenty20](/wiki/Twenty20 "Twenty20") cricket tournament [Indian Premier League](/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League") (IPL) for US$75.09 million, and named the team [Kolkata Knight Riders](/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") (KKR).[[251]](#cite_note-price-257) As of 2009[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shah_Rukh_Khan&action=edit), KKR was one of the richest teams in the IPL, with a brand value of US$42.1 million.[[252]](#cite_note-258) The team performed poorly on the field during the first three years.[[253]](#cite_note-major-259) Their performance improved over time, and they became the champions for the first time in [2012](/wiki/2012_Indian_Premier_League "2012 Indian Premier League")[[253]](#cite_note-major-259) and repeated the feat in [2014](/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League "2014 Indian Premier League").[[254]](#cite_note-260) The Knight Riders hold the record for the longest winning streak by any Indian team in T20s (14).[[255]](#cite_note-261) They won their third IPL title in the [2024](/wiki/2024_Indian_Premier_League "2024 Indian Premier League") edition.[[256]](#cite_note-262)

title: Shah Rukh Khan
text:
### Appearances in music videos

In February 2019, Khan made a special appearance in the music video of the song "BIBA", featuring [Marshmello](/wiki/Marshmello "Marshmello") and [Shirley Setia](/wiki/Shirley_Setia "Shirley Setia"), and composed by [Pritam](/wiki/Pritam "Pritam"). The video, inspired by Khan's memorable films, received positive response from fans, and Khan's cameo was well received.[[266]](#cite_note-272)

In June 2025, Khan appeared in the music video for the [Ed Sheeran](/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran") song "[Sapphire](/wiki/Sapphire_(song) "Sapphire (song)")", which also featured vocals from [Arijit Singh](/wiki/Arijit_Singh "Arijit Singh").[[267]](#cite_note-273) The video was shot across various parts of India, and the song received acclaim from critics and fans.[[268]](#cite_note-274)

Khan receives a considerable amount of media coverage in India, and is often referred to as "King Khan", "The [Baadshah](/wiki/Padishah "Padishah") of Bollywood", or "The King of Bollywood".[[b]](#cite_note-King-4) [Anupama Chopra](/wiki/Anupama_Chopra "Anupama Chopra") cites him as an "ever present celebrity", with two or three films a year, constantly running television ads, print ads, and gigantic billboards lining the streets of Indian cities.[[274]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChopra2007160–161-280) He is the object of a sometimes fanatical following, with a fan base estimated to exceed one billion.[[275]](#cite_note-TheAus-281) *[Newsweek](/wiki/Newsweek "Newsweek")* named Khan as one of their fifty most powerful people globally in 2008 and called him "the world's biggest movie star".[[276]](#cite_note-newsweek-282)[[277]](#cite_note-rediff.com-283) In 2011 he was described as "the biggest movie star you've never heard of ... perhaps the world's biggest movie star, period" by Steven Zeitchik of the *[Los Angeles Times](/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")*[[g]](#cite_note-285)[[279]](#cite_note-LAT-286) and has been called the world's biggest movie star in other international media outlets.[[c]](#cite_note-biggest-7) According to a popularity survey, 3.2 billion people around the world know Khan, more than who know [Tom Cruise](/wiki/Tom_Cruise "Tom Cruise").[[283]](#cite_note-billion-290) In a 2022 readers' poll by *[Empire](/wiki/Empire_(magazine) "Empire (magazine)")* magazine, Khan was listed as one of the 50 greatest actors of all time.

text:
Khan is one of the wealthiest celebrities in India, topping the *Forbes* India's "Celebrity 100 list" in 2012, 2013 and 2015.[[288]](#cite_note-forbes_100-295)[[289]](#cite_note-296)[[290]](#cite_note-297) His wealth has been estimated at US$1.4 billion.[[291]](#cite_note-BBC_Oct2025-298) Khan owns several properties in India and abroad, including a [£](/wiki/Pound_sterling "Pound sterling")20 million apartment in London,[[292]](#cite_note-299) and a villa on the [Palm Jumeirah](/wiki/Palm_Jumeirah "Palm Jumeirah") in [Dubai](/wiki/Dubai "Dubai").[[293]](#cite_note-300) From 2023–2024, Khan ranked as the highest tax payer in India.[[294]](#cite_note-301) In July 2026, Khan acquired the second and third floors of his former family home in Panchsheel Park, South Delhi, for approximately ₹37 crore, becoming the solo owner of the property where he and Gauri Khan had lived before his move to Mumbai.[[295]](#cite_note-302)

Khan frequently appears on listings of the most popular, stylish and influential people in India.

He has regularly featured among the top ten on *The Times of India*'s list of the 50 most desirable men in India,[[296]](#cite_note-303)[[297]](#cite_note-304) and in a 2007 poll by the magazine *[Eastern Eye](/wiki/Eastern_Eye "Eastern Eye")* he was named the sexiest man in Asia.[[298]](#cite_note-305) Khan is often referred to as "Brand SRK" by media organisations because of his many brand endorsement and entrepreneurship ventures.[[299]](#cite_note-rediffbrands-306)[[300]](#cite_note-bsrk-307) He is one of the highest paid Bollywood endorsers and one of the most visible celebrities in television advertising, with up to a six per cent share of the television advertisement market.[[301]](#cite_note-empire-308)[[302]](#cite_note-morebrands-309) Khan has endorsed brands including [Pepsi](/wiki/Pepsi "Pepsi"), [Nokia](/wiki/Nokia "Nokia"), [Hyundai](/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_Company "Hyundai Motor Company"), [Dish TV](/wiki/Dish_TV "Dish TV"), D'decor, [LUX](/wiki/Lux_(soap) "Lux (soap)") and [TAG Heuer](/wiki/TAG_Heuer "TAG Heuer").[[302]](#cite_note-morebrands-309)[[303]](#cite_note-Brands-310) Books have been published about him,[[304]](#cite_note-311)[[305]](#cite_note-312) and his popularity has been documented in several non-fiction films, including the two-part documentary *[The Inner and Outer World of Shah Rukh Khan](/wiki/The_Inner_and_Outer_World_of_Shah_Rukh_Khan "The Inner and Outer World of Shah Rukh Khan")* (2005),[[306]](#cite_note-world-313) and the [Discovery Travel & Living](/wiki/Discovery_Travel_%26_Living_(Europe) "Discovery Travel & Living (Europe)") channel's ten-part miniseries *Living with a Superstar—Shah Rukh Khan* (2010).[[301]](#cite_note-empire-308) In 2007, Khan became the third Indian actor to have his wax statue installed at London's [Madame Tussauds](/wiki/Madame_Tussauds "Madame Tussauds") museum, after Aishwarya Rai and Amitabh Bachchan.[[307]](#cite_note-314)[[308]](#cite_note-315) Additional versions of the statue were installed at Madame Tussauds' museums in Los Angeles, Hong Kong, New York and Washington.[[309]](#cite_note-316)

Khan has been brand ambassador of various governmental campaigns, including [Pulse Polio](/wiki/Pulse_Polio "Pulse Polio") and the [National AIDS Control Organisation](/wiki/National_AIDS_Control_Organisation "National AIDS Control Organisation").[[303]](#cite_note-Brands-310) He is a member of the board of directors of the [Make-A-Wish Foundation](/wiki/Make-A-Wish_Foundation "Make-A-Wish Foundation") in India,[[310]](#cite_note-317) and in 2011 he was appointed by [UNOPS](/wiki/UNOPS "UNOPS") as the first global ambassador of the [Water Supply and Sanitation Collaborative Council](/wiki/Water_Supply_and_Sanitation_Collaborative_Council "Water Supply and Sanitation Collaborative Council").[[311]](#cite_note-318) He has recorded a series of public service announcements championing good health and proper nutrition, and joined India's Health Ministry and [UNICEF](/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF") in a nationwide child immunisation campaign.[[312]](#cite_note-ihr-319) In 2011, he received [UNESCO](/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO")'s Pyramide con Marni award for his charitable commitment to provide education for children, becoming the first Indian to win the accolade.[[313]](#cite_note-Pyramide-320) In 2014, Khan became the ambassador for Interpol's campaign "Turn Back Crime".[[314]](#cite_note-321) In 2015, Khan received a privileged degree from the [University of Edinburgh](/wiki/University_of_Edinburgh "University of Edinburgh"), Scotland.[[315]](#cite_note-322) In 2018, Khan was honoured by the [World Economic Forum](/wiki/World_Economic_Forum "World Economic Forum") with their annual Crystal Award for his leadership in championing children's and women's rights in India.[[316]](#cite_note-323)[[317]](#cite_note-324)

In October 2019, Khan featured in a video launched by Prime Minister [Narendra Modi](/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi") to pay tribute to [Mahatma Gandhi](/wiki/Mahatma_Gandhi "Mahatma Gandhi") on his 150th birth anniversary. The preview of the video, which took place on 20 October 2019 at [PMO](/wiki/Prime_Minister%27s_Office_(India) "Prime Minister's Office (India)"), was attended by Khan, along with [Aamir Khan](/wiki/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan"), [Kangana Ranaut](/wiki/Kangana_Ranaut "Kangana Ranaut"), [Rajkumar Hirani](/wiki/Rajkumar_Hirani "Rajkumar Hirani"), [Jacqueline Fernandez](/wiki/Jacqueline_Fernandez "Jacqueline Fernandez"), [Sonam Kapoor](/wiki/Sonam_Kapoor "Sonam Kapoor"), [Ekta Kapoor](/wiki/Ekta_Kapoor "Ekta Kapoor"), [Varun Sharma](/wiki/Varun_Sharma "Varun Sharma"), [Jackie Shroff](/wiki/Jackie_Shroff "Jackie Shroff"), [Imtiaz Ali](/wiki/Imtiaz_Ali_(director) "Imtiaz Ali (director)"), [Sonu Nigam](/wiki/Sonu_Nigam "Sonu Nigam"), [Kapil Sharma](/wiki/Kapil_Sharma "Kapil Sharma"), and many other dignitaries.[[318]](#cite_note-325)[[319]](#cite_note-326)[[320]](#cite_note-327) Khan's distinctive voice and mannerisms have inspired many imitators and voice actors.[[321]](#cite_note-328) In the Hindi-dubbed version of the cartoon series *[Oggy and the Cockroaches](/wiki/Oggy_and_the_Cockroaches "Oggy and the Cockroaches")*, Saurav Chakrabarti emulates Khan's voice for the character Oggy.[[322]](#cite_note-329)

In April 2020, Khan announced a series of initiatives to help the government of India and the state governments of Maharashtra, West Bengal, and Delhi mitigate the [COVID-19 pandemic](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") as well as relief measures for thousands of underprivileged people and daily wage labourers affected by the [lockdown](/wiki/2020_coronavirus_lockdown_in_India "2020 coronavirus lockdown in India").[[323]](#cite_note-330)[[324]](#cite_note-331) He offered his 4-storey personal office space to the [Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation](/wiki/Brihanmumbai_Municipal_Corporation "Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation") to be used as a quarantine centre for coronavirus patients.[[325]](#cite_note-332)

On 5 May 2025, Khan attended the [Met Gala](/wiki/Met_Gala "Met Gala") in [Manhattan](/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), becoming the first Bollywood male actor to do so and making his debut appearance.[[326]](#cite_note-333) His outfit was designed by fashion designer [Sabyasachi Mukherjee](/wiki/Sabyasachi_Mukherjee "Sabyasachi Mukherjee").[[327]](#cite_note-334)

## Awards and recognitions

Main article: [List of awards and nominations received by Shah Rukh Khan](/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Shah_Rukh_Khan "List of awards and nominations received by Shah Rukh Khan")

Khan is one of the most decorated Bollywood actors.[[58]](#cite_note-toi-awards-64) He has received 14 [Filmfare Awards](/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards") from 30 nominations and special awards,[[328]](#cite_note-335)[[h]](#cite_note-ffan-336) including winning eight for Best Actor; he is tied for the most in this category with [Dilip Kumar](/wiki/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar").[[156]](#cite_note-FF8-162) Khan has won the [Filmfare Award for Best Actor](/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Actor") for his performances in *[Baazigar](/wiki/Baazigar "Baazigar")* (1993), *[Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge](/wiki/Dilwale_Dulhania_Le_Jayenge "Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge")* (1995), *[Dil To Pagal Hai](/wiki/Dil_To_Pagal_Hai "Dil To Pagal Hai")* (1997), *[Kuch Kuch Hota Hai](/wiki/Kuch_Kuch_Hota_Hai "Kuch Kuch Hota Hai")* (1998), *[Devdas](/wiki/Devdas_(2002_Hindi_film) "Devdas (2002 Hindi film)")* (2002), *[Swades](/wiki/Swades "Swades")* (2004), *[Chak De! India](/wiki/Chak_De!_India "Chak De! India")* (2007) and *[My Name Is Khan](/wiki/My_Name_Is_Khan "My Name Is Khan")* (2010).[[67]](#cite_note-FFAwardsPDF-73) He also won the [National Film Award for Best Actor in a Leading Role](/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Leading_Role "National Film Award for Best Actor in a Leading Role") in 2025 for his performance in [*Jawan*](/wiki/Jawan_(film) "Jawan (film)").[[216]](#cite_note-:4-222)

Khan was awarded the [Padma Shri](/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") by the [Government of India](/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") in 2005.[[58]](#cite_note-toi-awards-64) The [Government of France](/wiki/Government_of_France "Government of France") has awarded him both the [Order of Arts and Letters](/wiki/Ordre_des_Arts_et_des_Lettres "Ordre des Arts et des Lettres") (2007),[[329]](#cite_note-337) and the fifth degree of the French [Legion of Honour](/wiki/Legion_of_Honour "Legion of Honour"), *Chevalier de la Légion d'honneur* (2014).[[330]](#cite_note-338) Khan has received five honorary doctorates; the first from The [University of Bedfordshire](/wiki/University_of_Bedfordshire "University of Bedfordshire") in 2009,[[331]](#cite_note-339) the second from The [University of Edinburgh](/wiki/University_of_Edinburgh "University of Edinburgh") in 2015,[[332]](#cite_note-340) the third from [Maulana Azad National Urdu University](/wiki/Maulana_Azad_National_Urdu_University "Maulana Azad National Urdu University") in 2016,[[333]](#cite_note-341) and his latest from The [University of Law](/wiki/University_of_Law "University of Law") and [La Trobe University](/wiki/La_Trobe_University "La Trobe University") in 2019.[[334]](#cite_note-342)[[335]](#cite_note-343)

Khan married [Gauri Chibber](/wiki/Gauri_Khan "Gauri Khan"), a [Punjabi Hindu](/wiki/Punjabi_Hindu "Punjabi Hindu"), in a traditional Hindu wedding ceremony on 25 October 1991, after a six-year courtship.[[336]](#cite_note-344)[[337]](#cite_note-345) They have a son [Aryan](/wiki/Aryan_Khan "Aryan Khan") (born 1997)[[338]](#cite_note-346) and a daughter [Suhana](/wiki/Suhana_Khan "Suhana Khan") (born 2000).[[339]](#cite_note-347) In 2013, they became parents of a third child named AbRam,[[340]](#cite_note-348) who was born through a surrogate mother.[[341]](#cite_note-349) Both of his elder children have made their debut in the entertainment industry; Khan has stated that Aryan studied filmmaking at the [USC School of Cinematic Arts](/wiki/USC_School_of_Cinematic_Arts "USC School of Cinematic Arts") in [California](/wiki/California "California"), co-wrote and directed a Netflix series titled *[The Ba***ds of Bollywood](/wiki/The_Ba***ds_of_Bollywood "The Ba***ds of Bollywood")*,[[342]](#cite_note-350)[[343]](#cite_note-351) while Suhana, who served as assistant director for Khan's film *[Zero](/wiki/Zero_(2018_film) "Zero (2018 film)")* (2018), has studied drama and acting at [NYU's Tisch School of the Arts](/wiki/New_York_University_Tisch_School_of_the_Arts "New York University Tisch School of the Arts").

She made her debut in the Netflix film *[The Archies](/wiki/The_Archies_(film) "The Archies (film)")*.[[344]](#cite_note-352)[[345]](#cite_note-353) Suhana made her acting debut in November 2019, in a short film titled *The Grey Part of Blue*.[[346]](#cite_note-354) According to Khan, while he strongly believes in [Islam](/wiki/Islam "Islam"), he also values his wife's religion. His children follow both religions; at his home the [Qur'an](/wiki/Qur%27an "Qur'an") is situated next to the [murti](/wiki/Murti "Murti") of [Hindu](/wiki/Hindu "Hindu") deities.[[347]](#cite_note-355)

As of October 2025, Khan has a net worth of $1.4 billion.[[291]](#cite_note-BBC_Oct2025-298)
